replay.all_skipped: all %(count)d facts declare replay=False with no witness and no calibration ⇒ this gate checked nothing — keep at least one replayable fact; for expensive facts attach a witness (issue #5) so their provenance is checked on every commit; if the whole repo does not apply, set REFLECT_REPLAY=off and say so (a blanket exemption is not a pass)
replay.bad_timeout: REFLECT_REPLAY_TIMEOUT=%(value)r is not a number ⇒ using the default %(default).0fs
replay.calibrate_command_failed: `%(key)s` instrument calibration **command failed** (rc=%(return_code)s): `%(command)s` — the calibration command itself is dead (a calibration must be cheap, harmless, read-only)
replay.calibrate_mismatch: `%(key)s` instrument calibration mismatch: calibrate=%(actual)s vs expected=%(expected)s — the instrument is distorted (command succeeds, value is stable, replay always "passes", yet it may not be measuring what you think; first prove the instrument can see X using a known sample that contains X, then count)
replay.calibrate_timeout: `%(key)s` instrument calibration **timed out** (%(seconds).0fs): `%(command)s` — a calibration must be cheap; an expensive calibration is no calibration at all
replay.empty_ledger: ledger is empty — empty is not a pass (zero-value guard): check whether measure() is broken
replay.ledger_missing: fact ledger (%(name)s) is missing. Run python3 zreflect/facts.py to measure first.
replay.mismatch: `%(key)s` replay output does not match the ledger: stdout=%(actual)s vs ledger=%(expected)s — the fix is to **re-measure**: python3 zreflect/facts.py, then accept the change per-key with `--accept-changes=k1,k2`; if it still mismatches after re-measuring, then the cmd violates the bare-value contract (stdout may only print the value itself)
replay.no_cmd: `%(key)s` has no replay command — a fact without a cmd is prose (the bare-value contract requires it to have a cmd)
replay.none_ran: %(attempts)d attempts replayed and **not a single one succeeded** (all rc≠0 / timeout) — when the environment or shell is broken overall, per-entry errors masquerade as "all the data was checked" (zero-value guard)
replay.off: Replay gate: REFLECT_REPLAY=off ⇒ this gate is disabled (stated, not pretended as checked — for the few entries that need build artifacts use replay=False individually, do not turn off the whole gate)
replay.ok: Replay gate: OK (%(count)d facts replayed verbatim; stdout matches the ledger%(skipped)s%(witnessed)s%(calibrated)s)
replay.ok_skipped: , %(count)d declared replay=False and were not run
replay.principle_is_off: principle `%(key)s` came back **off** (not enabled): %(detail)s — off is not a pass. Command: %(command)s
replay.principle_said_nothing: principle `%(key)s` answered with **nothing** (empty stdout) — that cannot be told apart from 'never ran'. Command: %(command)s
replay.timeout: `%(key)s` replay **timed out** (%(seconds).0fs): `%(command)s` — entries that need to start services or build should set replay=False, do not treat a timeout as data. Note: after a reboot the first cold-start run may time out (cold filesystem; it usually returns in a second once caches are warm) — rerun once before judging, or raise REFLECT_REPLAY_TIMEOUT
replay.title: Replay gate
replay.too_deep: replay nesting too deep (depth %(depth)d, limit %(limit)d) — commands in the ledger form a cycle: some principle's cmd triggers replay again. Fix the ledger; do not raise the limit
replay.witness_command_failed: `%(key)s` witness **command failed** (rc=%(return_code)s): `%(command)s` — the witness command itself is dead (a witness must be cheap, harmless, read-only)
replay.witness_mismatch: `%(key)s` witness mismatch: witness=%(actual)s vs expected=%(expected)s — provenance/context drift (the tool or input that produced it changed); the value itself not changing still **counts as an incident**
replay.witness_timeout: `%(key)s` witness **timed out** (%(seconds).0fs): `%(command)s` — a witness must be cheap; an expensive witness is no witness at all
